summary: Use a Thread Hero at the top of a payment or chat thread to show who the other person is: their name, banking name, and number.

examples.purpose: The top of a payment thread, the guide's In context: the hero names the person (their initials in a Monogram Avatar, the name people know, the labelled banking name and their number) before the payments below it. The thread lays it out and shows the payments.
examples.jsx:
<ThreadHero
  renderAvatar={<Avatar style="Monogram" monogram="RV" />}
  title="Rahul Verma"
  subtitle="Banking name: RAHUL KUMAR VERMA"
  caption="+91 98765 43210"
/>

from.quote: The hero opens the thread, so people know who they’re paying before they see the payments below it.

examples.purpose: Without a banking name: an empty subtitle hides the line (left out, the hero would show its default banking name).
examples.jsx:
<ThreadHero
  renderAvatar={<Avatar style="Monogram" monogram="RV" />}
  title="Rahul Verma"
  subtitle=""
  caption="+91 98765 43210"
/>

from.quote: An empty subtitle hides the line.

examples.purpose: A long name, the guide's Wrapped state: the name wraps anyway, and disableTruncation lets the banking name and the UPI ID wrap too instead of ending in an ellipsis.
examples.jsx:
<ThreadHero
  renderAvatar={<Avatar style="Monogram" monogram="VR" />}
  title="Venkatasubramanian Ramakrishnan"
  subtitle="Banking name: VENKATASUBRAMANIAN RAMAKRISHNAN"
  caption="venkatasubramanian.r@okjio"
  disableTruncation
/>

from.quote: disableTruncation lets them wrap too.

props.name: title
props.description: The name: 16 px Semibold (600) on a 20 px line, centred; it wraps, with no line limit. Declared: Title text, e.g. "Subhash Rajan". Default "Subhash Rajan", from the component source.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: The banking name: 12 px Medium on an 18 px line, grey, centred, one line with an ellipsis. An empty string hides it; left out, it shows the default. Declared: Subtitle text, e.g. "Banking name: SHIVASHANKAR RAJAN". Default "Banking name: SHIVASHANKAR RAJAN", from the component source.

props.name: caption
props.description: No default: 12 px Medium on an 18 px line, grey, one line with an ellipsis, 8 px below the banking name; hidden when not passed. Declared: Optional caption text below the details, e.g. "+91 00000 00000".

props.name: renderAvatar
props.description: No default avatar. The avatar gets the hero's modes and its own modes win; fragments and arrays get the hero's modes too; false shows no avatar. Declared: Slot for Avatar component.

props.name: modes
props.description: No mode changes the hero's own text: its tokens have one mode. The hero passes its modes to the avatar. Declared: Modes for design token resolution.

props.name: disableTruncation
props.description: The banking name and the caption wrap instead of ending in an ellipsis; the name wraps either way. Declared: When `true`, disables text truncation: the trailing ellipsis (`…`) is never shown and any `numberOfLines` clamp is ignored, so the text wraps to as many lines as it needs even when horizontal space is tight.

modes.name: Avatar Size
modes.description: Not read by the hero's own text: the hero passes its modes to the avatar, so Avatar Size on the hero sizes it (a hero at S gives a 29 px avatar), and an Avatar Size set on the avatar itself wins (an avatar at M gives 36 px whatever the hero's size). Figma's nested Avatar is 42 px.

gaps.text: Figma's Thread Hero has Title, Subtitle and Caption text properties, a caption switch and a nested Avatar; the package has no avatar unless you pass one in renderAvatar.
Figma's caption shows by default and its Thread Hero is 360 px wide; the package hides the caption until you pass one and has no width of its own (it hugs its text).
